text: showed that hybrid solar+sulfur TES+NG boiler systems are economically competitive with incumbent natural gas boilers for multiple locations in the southwest US. The project also generated the first unsubsidized, paid purchase orders for engineering design of a sulfur TES pilot integrated with solar thermal for enhanced oil recovery. In addition, Element 16 was awarded funding from the California Energy Commission to deploy a sulfur TES pilot at a large industrial facility to support transition from coal cogeneration to solar energy. This project expands understanding of molten sulfur as a cost-effective, durable, and scalable thermal storage medium. Results demonstrate both technical effectiveness and economic feasibility, validating sulfur TES as a practical solution for decarbonizing medium-temperature IPH. The broader public benefits include: Environmental: lower GHG emissions, Economic: more stable and lower IPH costs that enhance U.S. manufacturing competitiveness, Energy security: reduced reliance on imported natural gas, Health and safety: reduced nitrous oxide and other combustion emissions that pose public health risks. In summary, this project established molten sulfur TES as a technically viable and economically competitive pathway to accelerate the decarbonization of industrial process heat in the United States.
